name: Battle of Midway

phases.title: The fleets take their places
phases.text: Nimitz sent Fletcher's force to the Midway area before the Japanese arrived, and the two American task forces waited northeast of the atoll. Nagumo's carriers approached from the west, with Yamamoto's ships several hundred miles behind them.

phases.title: The Japanese strike Midway, and Midway's bombers strike back
phases.text: Nagumo launched his first attack on Midway at 04:30. Bombers that had taken off from the atoll before the Japanese arrived attacked his carriers. The Japanese repelled them, and the strike on Midway left its defences largely intact.

phases.title: American torpedo squadrons are shot down
phases.text: The American carriers had launched from 07:00, and their torpedo squadrons reached the Japanese carriers without fighter escort. Most were shot down and none of their torpedoes hit, but the attacks drew the Japanese fighters out of position.

phases.title: Dive bombers hit three of the four carriers
phases.text: Dive bombers from Enterprise and Yorktown arrived while the Japanese fighters were drawn off. Kaga and Akagi were hit and set on fire, and Sōryū was hit too. All three were eventually abandoned and scuttled.

phases.title: Hiryū strikes Yorktown
phases.text: Hiryū, the one carrier still operating, sent two waves after the American aircraft. Three bombs hit Yorktown in the first, and two torpedoes crippled her in the second. Fletcher moved his command staff to the cruiser Astoria.

phases.title: Enterprise's bombers cripple Hiryū
phases.text: A Yorktown scout found Hiryū, and Enterprise launched 24 dive bombers. Four bombs, possibly five, hit her and left her ablaze. She stayed afloat for several hours and sank after being spotted the next morning.

phases.title: Both sides draw back
phases.text: Spruance withdrew to the east during the night, fearing a night encounter with Japanese surface ships. Yamamoto had detached a cruiser force to bombard Midway, then ordered a general withdrawal to the west, and the cruisers turned back.

note: The plan shows the whole operation, not a single field: each block is a fleet or a group of carriers, and the distances are schematic. Only the directions the account gives are kept: the Americans lay northeast of Midway and east of Nagumo's carriers, and Yamamoto's ships trailed Nagumo by several hundred miles. The attack groups of aircraft are drawn as arrows between the fleets that sent them.
